verses.1: The heart of a king is like streams of water, in the hand of the LORD. In every direction he desires, he turns it.
verses.2: Every way a person seems just in their own eyes, but the LORD weighs the hearts.
verses.3: Doing righteousness and justice is more pleasing to the LORD than a sacrifice.
verses.4: A proud look and a haughty heart are a lamp for the wicked — their sin is glaring.
verses.5: Plans are like a net to the one who is ready, and every wise man is ready for abundance.
verses.6: One who makes false promises with their tongue pursues emptiness — seekers of death are those who chase it.
verses.7: The spoil of the wicked brings ruin, for they refuse to do justice.
verses.8: The crooked paths are twisted, but the upright man’s deeds are straight.
verses.9: It is better to dwell on the roof of a house than to share a house with a quarrelsome woman and her strife.
verses.10: A wicked person’s soul desires evil — in their eyes, no one is innocent.
verses.11: The punishment of a scoffer teaches a fool, and the discerning man gains knowledge.
verses.12: The discerning man knows the heart of the wicked — and turns the wicked to evil.
verses.13: One who stops their ears to the cry of the poor — they too will cry out, but no one will answer.
verses.14: A gift given in secret calms anger, and a bribe in the bosom brings strong wrath.
verses.15: Joy to the righteous in doing justice, and a curse to the workers of iniquity.
verses.16: A man who wanders from the path of understanding will rest in the assembly of the dead.
verses.17: A man who is poor loves mirth — he who loves wine and oil will not be rich.
verses.18: A ransom for the righteous is the wicked, and a substitute for the upright is the deceiver.
verses.19: It is better to live in the wilderness than with a quarrelsome and angry woman.
verses.20: A treasure is precious, and oil in the dwelling of the wise — but fools consume it.
verses.21: One who pursues righteousness and steadfast love will find life — righteousness and honor.
verses.22: A wise man climbs the walls of strong cities and brings down the fortress in which the wicked had trusted.
verses.23: One who guards their mouth and their tongue guards their life from troubles.
verses.24: A scoffer who is arrogant — his name is Zed, and he acts through deceit.
verses.25: The desires of the lazy will kill them, for their hands refuse to work.
verses.26: The wicked crave all day long for evil, but the righteous gives and does not withhold.
verses.27: The sacrifice of the wicked is an abomination — for they bring it with deceit.
verses.28: A false witness will be destroyed, but the man who listens faithfully will speak.
verses.29: A wicked man dares with his face, but the upright man understands his way.
verses.30: There is no wisdom, no understanding, no counsel against the LORD.
verses.31: A horse is prepared for the day of battle — but salvation is from the LORD.

notes:
Notes
- v. 4: "nir reshaim chata’at" — the phrase is ambiguous. The rendering assumes "a lamp for the wicked — their sin is glaring," where "nir" is a lamp and "reshaim" the wicked.
- v. 24: "zad yahir leitz shemo" — "Zed" is a name possibly derived from "zad" (deceit) or an otherwise unattested term; the name remains speculative but is rendered as "Zed" to preserve the Hebrew nuance.
- v. 27: "zavach resha'im to'evah ki be-zimah yevi'enu" — "the sacrifice of the wicked is an abomination — for they bring it with deceit." "Be-zimah" is a rare term, meaning "with deceit" or "in a conspiracy."
